name: text-overflow
title: Text overflow and ellipsis
summary: The same long sentence in 120 dp boxes, cut after 1, 2 and 3 lines with an end ellipsis, on one line with start and middle ellipses, and clipped with no mark.
prompt: Show how a long sentence is truncated in a narrow box: maxLines 1, 2 and 3 with an ellipsis, plus start and middle ellipsis and plain clipping.
teaches: Clamp a text to N lines with maxLines and mark the cut with overflow "ellipsis"
Keep the end of a string visible with overflow "start_ellipsis", or both ends with "middle_ellipsis"
Give the text a fixed width (a width modifier on the text itself) so it has something to overflow

snippets.note: maxLines 2, overflow ellipsis, in a 120 dp width

check.describe: Rows 1–3 show 1, 2 and 3 lines ending in …; the start_ellipsis row begins with … and shows the sentence's end; the middle_ellipsis row has … in the middle; the clip row is cut without a mark. Resized: the caption column takes the remaining width (weight 1), so at 240 the captions crowd the 120 dp sample boxes without overlapping, and at 540 the boxes sit at the right edge. (C++ player: at other widths the maxLines 2/3 boxes show fewer lines — it counts lines against the row width, not the 120 dp box.)

pitfalls: overflow defaults to clip, which cuts mid-letter with no mark: ask for "ellipsis" explicitly
An ellipsis needs a bound: without maxLines the text just wraps onto more lines, and without a bounded width (width, fillMaxWidth or a weight) it grows to fit and never overflows
start_ellipsis and middle_ellipsis are meant for a single line (as on Android, where multi-line start/middle truncation is not supported): use them with maxLines 1
The width modifier includes the text's own padding: width 120 with padding 4 leaves 112 dp for the letters
